lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 6, which colour does a layered print use first? (The lightest.) Today: woodcuts, and the Japanese way of printing with wood blocks.
A woodcut is a relief print: you cut away what should stay white, and the raised parts left standing take the ink and print dark.
The print comes out mirrored, because the paper lies face down on the block. So letters must be carved back to front.
Worked example: this block's raised parts form an R carved back to front. Printed, it turns round and reads the right way.
Tools: a V-gouge cuts thin lines and a U-gouge clears wide areas. Always cut away from your body, keep your other hand behind the blade, and hold the wood still on a bench hook.

In Japan, ukiyo-e prints used a key block for the black outlines, then one block for each colour. The blocks were lined up with marks called kento. Ink was brushed on, and the paper rubbed with a flat pad, a baren.
Prints are made in editions and numbered in pencil: 7/25 means print 7 of 25. Albrecht Dürer (1471-1528) made his famous Rhinoceros woodcut in 1515 without ever seeing the animal.
Try it in the world: with a grown-up, carve a simple shape into half a potato or a foam sheet and print it. Did it come out mirrored? Next: curating a portfolio.

exercises.prompt: In a woodcut, which parts print dark?
exercises.hint: The roller only touches the highest parts.
exercises.explain: The raised parts take the ink and print; the cut parts stay white.

exercises.prompt: A woodcut print comes out mirrored, left to right.
exercises.hint: The paper lies face down on the block.
exercises.explain: True: what is on the left of the block prints on the right.

exercises.prompt: Which print does this block make?
exercises.hint: Turn the block over left to right in your head.
exercises.explain: The print is the block mirrored: the dark squares on the left of the block print on the right.

exercises.hint: Its blade is shaped like a letter.
exercises.explain: A V-gouge makes a thin, sharp line.

exercises.prompt: How should you cut with a gouge?
exercises.hint: Where would the blade go if it slipped?
choices: away from your body, hand behind the blade
with the wood held in the air
exercises.explain: Away from your body, with your other hand behind the blade and the wood held on a bench hook.

exercises.prompt: Which print does this block make?
exercises.hint: Mirror each row, left to right.
exercises.explain: Each row prints mirrored, so the shape faces the other way.

exercises.prompt: A print is numbered 7/25 in pencil. How many prints are in the edition?
exercises.hint: Which number is the edition's size?
exercises.explain: 7/25 means print 7 of an edition of 25.

exercises.hint: Japanese printers rubbed the back of the paper with it.
choices: a flat pad to rub the paper
exercises.explain: A baren is a flat pad for rubbing the paper onto the inked block.

exercises.prompt: Match each tool or word to its job.
exercises.hint: Two cut, one holds, one lines up, one presses.
exercises.explain: V-gouge: lines; U-gouge: wide areas; bench hook: holds; kento: lines up; baren: rubs.

exercises.prompt: Letters must be carved back to front to print the right way round.
exercises.explain: True: the print mirrors the block.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of making a woodcut in order.
items: press the paper and lift it off
cut away what should stay white
draw the design on the block
exercises.explain: Draw it, cut away the white parts, ink the raised parts, then press and lift the paper.

exercises.prompt: Which print does this block make?
exercises.explain: Each of the five rows is printed mirrored.

exercises.prompt: A Japanese-style print has black outlines and 3 colours. How many blocks does it need, with the key block?
exercises.hint: One block for the outlines, and one for each colour.

exercises.prompt: Why does each colour block have its kento marks in the same place?
exercises.hint: What goes wrong if the paper slips between colours?
choices: so each colour lines up on the paper
exercises.explain: The paper sits in the same kento marks on every block, so all the colours line up.

exercises.prompt: This block shows an R carved back to front. What does its print show?
choices: an R the right way round
exercises.explain: Mirroring a back-to-front R turns it the right way round.

exercises.prompt: Dürer carved his Rhinoceros woodcut after seeing the animal himself.
exercises.hint: Think of where rhinoceroses lived, and where Dürer did.
exercises.explain: False: he worked from a letter and a sketch sent from Lisbon, and never saw it.

exercises.prompt: Sort the parts of a woodcut block: prints dark, or stays white?
exercises.hint: Only the surface the roller touches takes the ink.
exercises.explain: Prints dark: the raised parts, the lines left standing and the uncut surface take the ink. Stays white: everything cut away, by a U-gouge or a V-gouge, sits too low for the ink.

exercises.prompt: Put the making of a Japanese colour print in order.
items: Rub the paper with a baren.
Carve one block for each colour.
Carve a key block for the outlines.
Line the paper up on the kento marks.
exercises.hint: The outlines come first, and every colour must land in the right place.
exercises.explain: Carve the key block for the black outlines, then one block for each colour. Line the paper up on the kento marks, rub it with a baren, and repeat for every colour block, so all the colours land in place.
